- If sentiment is consistently neutral (0.00) in recent history, model tends to overestimate early in horizon; correct by reducing initial forecast values by 1–2%.
- If sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.00) and model forecasts are rising, model often overshoots; cap upward revisions at +3% of recent 7-day average.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by downward correction, reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection lag.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60), model tends to hold too high; apply downward bias of 1–3% per day until trend stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, if model forecast is >68 and true outcome is >68, reduce forecast by 2–4% to avoid overestimating peak prices.
- If sentiment history includes a recent positive spike (e.g., 0.25), model often underestimates subsequent rally; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5 days.
